newsitem.title: CANADA: Alcan's 2nd-quarter profit up on higher shipments.
newsitem.headline: Alcan's 2nd-quarter profit up on higher shipments.

text.p: Alcan Aluminium Ltd.'s second-quarter earnings rose slightly on higher shipments, but fabricated product prices did not reflect the stronger aluminum ingot market, the company said on Thursday.
Second-quarter net profit at Montreal-based Alcan, the world's second largest aluminum producer, rose to $116 million or 50 cents a share from year earlier 112 million or 47 cents a share.
Sales climbed to $2.03 billion from $1.97 billion in the year ago quarter.
Total shipments of ingot and fabricated products rose 9.3 percent to 737,000 metric tons in the latest quarter from 674,000 tonnes a year earlier. First-quarter 1997 volume was 690,000 tonnes.
"Fabricated product prices, however, do not fully reflect the increase in aluminum ingot prices over the previous nine months," Alcan President Jacques Bougie said in a statement.
"Looking ahead, we continue to believe that improved aluminum demand in the major economies should support slightly higher aluminum prices by the end of this year," he said.
For the first six months, Alcan's earnings rose to $259 million or $1.12 a share from year earlier $237 million or $1 a share. First-half sales fell to $3.93 billion from $3.99 billion.
Manfred Mallory of Research Capital Corp., said analysts would likely lower their full-year earnings forecasts for Alcan.
"My old forecast was $2.45 a share, but I think it clearly is going to come in less than that," Mallory said. In 1996 Alcan earned $410 million or $1.74 a share.
Alcan closed down C40 cents to C$47.95 on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Thursday. In New York, Alcan fell 25 cents to $34.875.
